title: Specify scroll restoration in a bit more detail
body:
Currently the spec performs scroll restoration at the end of [traverse the history](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#traverse-the-history), between popstate and hashchange. There are even [passing tests for this](https://wpt.fyi/results/html/browsers/browsing-the-web/history-traversal/scroll-restoration-order.html?label=master&label=experimental&aligned).

However, the full story here is a bit more complicated. From what I've been told by Chromium engineers, and from black-box testing in Firefox, it appears that this is really a point at which scroll restoration _starts being attempted_. If attempting to restore scroll position at this time doesn't work, then the browser will continue trying for some time, as new content loads. This demo site shows what I mean: https://neat-equal-cent.glitch.me/

I don't think we need to fully specify everything here. For example, let's say you use the demo site as it suggests and scroll down to paragraph 100. Right now on the demo site Firefox will continually keep you scrolled to the bottom of the page as new content loads, until paragraph 100 appears and it stops. Whereas Chrome will not do any scrolling until paragraph 100 loads, and then it will do a single jump. These differences seem like reasonable user experience choices browsers could differ on.

But we should:

- Be clear that "restore scroll position" is the start of the process, not a one-time thing
- Say that browsers should (may? must?) discontinue the scroll restoration process if the user scrolls the viewport
- Maybe mention the connection to [scroll anchoring](https://github.com/WICG/ScrollAnchoring/blob/master/explainer.md), i.e., mention the fact that even once scroll restoration is "done", there may be further scroll events fired by scroll anchoring
